title: Deep Dives
lede: Quantify the game on the fly. Each dive is an empirical answer built from thousands of WNBA games — read-only analysis, baked to static numbers, honest about its uncertainty.

dives.title: The two-seed race has no head-to-heads left
dives.one_line: Golden State Valkyries and Las Vegas Aces never play again - the seed is settled by venue, rest, and two games against Minnesota.
dives.question: What decides a two-team race with no games left between them?

dives.title: The deserved standings
dives.one_line: Washington Mystics are about 3.6 wins ahead of what they have earned; Seattle Storm are 6.6 behind - and are 0-13 in close games.
dives.question: Which teams have earned their record?

dives.title: The Least Valuable Points in Basketball
dives.one_line: A team leading by 15+ in the fourth scores 105.01 per 100 against a 112.37 baseline for the same quarter — identical shot quality, 7.36 fewer points.
dives.question: Does scoring get easier once a game is decided?

dives.title: Even teams: scoreline odds by quarter
dives.one_line: Two evenly-matched teams — the odds of leading and winning at each quarter break.
dives.question: Even teams — odds of leading / winning at each quarter break?

dives.title: Comeback odds by deficit + time
dives.one_line: Trailing by N with T left — how often you come back to win.
dives.question: Down N with T left — win %?

dives.title: Home-court edge, decomposed
dives.one_line: Measured across 2792 games, home is worth +2.2 pts / 55.9%. Where does the edge actually come from?
dives.question: What is home worth, and why?

dives.title: Rest & back-to-back effects
dives.one_line: What a back-to-back costs a team, and whether stars get load-managed.
dives.question: How much does a rest edge / a B2B cost?

dives.title: Clutch: who rises and fades late
dives.one_line: Who shows up when it's close and late — the players and teams that rise or fade in the clutch.
dives.question: Who rises / fades in the clutch?

dives.title: Pace & possession value
dives.one_line: The fastest team runs ~7.4 more possessions a game than the slowest — but pace doesn't win; efficiency does.
dives.question: Does playing fast help you win?

dives.title: Scoring mix: twos, threes, and the line
dives.one_line: Golden State Valkyries get 39% of their points from three vs a 30% league average — but three-reliance is style, not a win driver.
dives.question: Where do a team's points come from, and does the mix win?

dives.title: The Mid-Range Is Dead. Long Live the Mid-Range.
dives.one_line: A mid-range jumper returns 0.79 points a shot; a three from 24-26 feet returns 1.04 — 31% more scoreboard for one step back.
dives.question: What does a shot return, by where it was taken?

dives.title: The W is playing deeper — and it's changing what can be predicted
dives.one_line: Teams are using 9.87 players a game, up from 9.43 — and minutes reliability fell from .905 to .695.
dives.question: How many players does a team actually use, and what does it break?

dives.title: How close are the games?
dives.one_line: About 1 in 7 games (14%) is a one-possession nailbiter and ~32% are decided by 6 or fewer -- but 15% are 20-point blowouts, and games are not getting closer.
dives.question: How close are the games, and are they getting closer?

dives.title: Scoring leaders: who is putting up points
dives.one_line: A'ja Wilson paces the league at 26.1 a game, while Chennedy Carter tops the efficiency board -- and Marina Mabrey's 53-point night is the season high.
dives.question: Who leads in scoring, who does it most efficiently, and what were the biggest single-game explosions?

dives.title: Score effects: playing ahead vs behind
dives.one_line: How pace, shot choice and fouling shift with the scoreboard state, and how the simulators could use it.
dives.question: How does a team play differently when it is ahead versus behind?

dives.title: Situation Explorer: what usually happens from here
dives.one_line: Set the score, the clock, the floor and the matchup - read what actually happened from that spot across a decade of real games. Down 6 entering the 4th on an even floor: teams came back 24.5% of the time (429 games).
dives.question: From this exact game situation - score, clock, floor, matchup - what usually happens?
